exercises.title: Exercise 1 — how tall is the tree? A 4-byte key vs a 200-byte key
exercises.problemHtml:
Estimate first: two tables of 200,000 rows each. KhoaHep(ma INT PRIMARY KEY) and KhoaRong(ma CHAR(200) PRIMARY KEY) holding the same numbers as text. How many levels does each clustered index have?

Then build both tables (one set-based INSERT each), and the view dbo.vTreeDepth(bang, so_tang) that reads the depth of each clustered index with INDEXPROPERTY(object_id, index_name, 'IndexDepth').

Runs on YOUR SQL Server, not in the browser. Tree depth is a property of SQL Server's own B+tree pages (INDEXPROPERTY … 'IndexDepth'); the browser grader has neither these pages nor this function. Nothing here is graded automatically: run the self-check check.sql on your machine and, when it prints ALL 3 CHECKS PASSED, press Mark as solved.

How to run it (Windows or macOS)

Press Tải .zip (download) above the code and unzip it. The folder has three files: setup.sql (re-creates a scratch database DBI202_CL with the sample tables), solution.sql (YOUR answer — edit only this one) and check.sql (3 checks; prints PASS/FAIL for each and ends with ALL 3 CHECKS PASSED). Always run them in this order: setup → solution → check.

  • Windows + SSMS (the course setup, lesson 0.3): open setup.sql → F5; open solution.sql → F5; open check.sql → F5, then read the Messages tab. Or in a terminal inside the folder (sqlcmd ships with SQL Server; otherwise winget install sqlcmd):
    sqlcmd -S localhost -E -C -i setup.sql,solution.sql,check.sql (use -U sa -P "<password>" instead of -E for a SQL login).
  • macOS (SQL Server in Docker, as in lesson 0.3 — Apple Silicon: mcr.microsoft.com/azure-sql-edge, Intel: mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2022-latest):
    docker run -d --name dbi202-sql -e ACCEPT_EULA=Y -e "MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD=Dbi202#Lab" -p 1433:1433 mcr.microsoft.com/azure-sql-edge
    then install the command-line client once with brew install sqlcmd and, inside the folder:
    sqlcmd -S localhost,1433 -U sa -P "Dbi202#Lab" -C -i setup.sql,solution.sql,check.sql
    (or open the three files in VS Code with the SQL Server (mssql) extension and run them in the same order).

Use CREATE OR ALTER for procedures, functions, triggers and views so that you can run solution.sql again and again. In the real PE you submit only the CREATE … statement, without GO or test commands.

Requirements

  • Both tables have exactly 200,000 rows, ma = 1…200000.
  • vTreeDepth: one row per table, the depth of index_id = 1.

Ước lượng trước: hai bảng mỗi bảng 200.000 dòng. KhoaHep(ma INT PRIMARY KEY) và KhoaRong(ma CHAR(200) PRIMARY KEY) chứa cùng các số dưới dạng chữ. Mỗi chỉ mục cụm có bao nhiêu tầng?

Rồi dựng hai bảng (mỗi bảng một câu INSERT theo tập) và view dbo.vTreeDepth(bang, so_tang) đọc độ sâu của từng chỉ mục cụm bằng INDEXPROPERTY(object_id, tên_chỉ_mục, 'IndexDepth').

Chạy trên SQL SERVER CỦA BẠN, không chạy trong trình duyệt. Độ sâu cây là thuộc tính của trang B+tree của chính SQL Server (INDEXPROPERTY … 'IndexDepth'); máy chấm trình duyệt không có các trang này lẫn hàm này. Trang này không tự chấm: chạy tệp tự kiểm check.sql trên máy bạn, khi nó in ALL 3 CHECKS PASSED thì bấm Tự đánh dấu đã giải.

Cách chạy (Windows hoặc macOS)

Bấm Tải .zip ở khung code rồi giải nén. Thư mục có ba tệp: setup.sql (tạo lại CSDL nháp DBI202_CL với các bảng mẫu), solution.sql (bài làm CỦA BẠN — chỉ sửa tệp này) và check.sql (3 kiểm; in PASS/FAIL từng kiểm và kết thúc bằng ALL 3 CHECKS PASSED). Luôn chạy đúng thứ tự: setup → solution → check.

  • Windows + SSMS (cài như bài 0.3): mở setup.sql → F5; mở solution.sql → F5; mở check.sql → F5, rồi đọc tab Messages. Hoặc mở terminal trong thư mục (sqlcmd đi kèm SQL Server; chưa có thì winget install sqlcmd):
    sqlcmd -S localhost -E -C -i setup.sql,solution.sql,check.sql (đăng nhập SQL thì thay -E bằng -U sa -P "<mật khẩu>").
  • macOS (SQL Server trong Docker như bài 0.3 — Apple Silicon: mcr.microsoft.com/azure-sql-edge, Intel: mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2022-latest):
    docker run -d --name dbi202-sql -e ACCEPT_EULA=Y -e "MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD=Dbi202#Lab" -p 1433:1433 mcr.microsoft.com/azure-sql-edge
    rồi cài trình dòng lệnh một lần bằng brew install sqlcmd và, trong thư mục bài:
    sqlcmd -S localhost,1433 -U sa -P "Dbi202#Lab" -C -i setup.sql,solution.sql,check.sql
    (hoặc mở ba tệp trong VS Code có extension SQL Server (mssql) và chạy đúng thứ tự đó).

Viết procedure, function, trigger, view bằng CREATE OR ALTER để chạy lại solution.sql bao nhiêu lần cũng được. Khi thi PE thật chỉ nộp lệnh CREATE …, không GO, không lệnh chạy thử.

  • Cả hai bảng có đúng 200.000 dòng, ma = 1…200000.
  • vTreeDepth: mỗi bảng một dòng, độ sâu của index_id = 1.

-- solution.sql — YOUR answer for: Exercise 1 — how tall is the tree? A 4-byte key vs a 200-byte key
-- Bài làm CỦA BẠN. Run order / thứ tự chạy: setup.sql → solution.sql → check.sql
USE DBI202_CL;
GO
CREATE TABLE dbo.KhoaHep  (ma INT       NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY);   -- 4-byte key
CREATE TABLE dbo.KhoaRong (ma CHAR(200) NOT NULL PRIMARY KEY);   -- 200-byte key, same numbers as text
GO
WITH n AS (
    SELECT TOP (200000) ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY (SELECT NULL)) AS rn
    FROM sys.all_columns a CROSS JOIN sys.all_columns b
)
INSERT INTO dbo.KhoaHep (ma) SELECT rn FROM n;
INSERT INTO dbo.KhoaRong (ma) SELECT CAST(ma AS CHAR(200)) FROM dbo.KhoaHep;
GO
CREATE OR ALTER VIEW dbo.vTreeDepth AS
SELECT OBJECT_NAME(i.object_id)                            AS bang,
       INDEXPROPERTY(i.object_id, i.name, 'IndexDepth')    AS so_tang
FROM sys.indexes i
WHERE i.object_id IN (OBJECT_ID(N'dbo.KhoaHep'), OBJECT_ID(N'dbo.KhoaRong')) AND i.index_id = 1;

exercises.solutionExplanationHtml: Same rows, twice the reads per seek (4 vs 2) — and every nonclustered index on KhoaRong would also carry the 200-byte key. That is the practical reason behind "keep the clustered key narrow".
exercises.solutionExplanationHtmlVi: Cùng số dòng, mỗi lần seek đọc gấp đôi (4 so với 2) — và mọi chỉ mục nonclustered trên KhoaRong còn mang theo khoá 200 byte. Đó là lý do thực tế của lời khuyên "giữ khoá cụm hẹp".

exercises.title: Exercise 2 — one index for three queries
exercises.problemHtml:
The "customer orders" screen sends three queries, always for one customer, all selecting ngayDat, tongTien:

  • WHERE khachHangId = @kh AND trangThai = 'XONG'
  • WHERE khachHangId = @kh ORDER BY ngayDat DESC
  • WHERE khachHangId = @kh AND ngayDat >= '2025-01-01'

Create ONE index ix_dh_kh_ngay that makes all three an Index Seek with no Key Lookup and no Sort.

DonHang(id PK, maDon, khachHangId, ngayDat DATE, trangThai XONG/HUY/CHO, tongTien) — 20 orders (a small copy of the lesson's 50,000-row table, with the edge cases kept); ChiTietDon(id PK, donHangId FK → DonHang, sanPham, soLuong).

Requirements

  • CREATE INDEX ix_dh_kh_ngay ON DonHang (…) INCLUDE (…);
  • Key columns in the right order; columns that are only filtered loosely or selected go to INCLUDE.

Tạo MỘT chỉ mục ix_dh_kh_ngay để cả ba đều là Index Seek, không Key Lookup, không Sort.

kiem.kiemTra:
SELECT lower(i.relname) AS chi_muc, lower(t.relname) AS bang, x.indisunique AS duy_nhat,
  (SELECT string_agg(lower(a.attname), ', ' ORDER BY k.n) FROM unnest(x.indkey::int2[]) WITH ORDINALITY AS k(attnum, n)
     JOIN pg_attribute a ON a.attrelid = x.indrelid AND a.attnum = k.attnum WHERE k.n <= x.indnkeyatts) AS cot_khoa,
  (SELECT string_agg(lower(a.attname), ', ' ORDER BY lower(a.attname)) FROM unnest(x.indkey::int2[]) WITH ORDINALITY AS k(attnum, n)
     JOIN pg_attribute a ON a.attrelid = x.indrelid AND a.attnum = k.attnum WHERE k.n > x.indnkeyatts) AS cot_include,
  lower(replace(pg_get_expr(x.indpred, x.indrelid), ' ', '')) AS dieu_kien

exercises.title: Exercise 5 — diagnose a slow query in six steps (50,000 orders)
exercises.problemHtml:
"Your orders this year" is slow. The app sends SELECT id, maDon, ngayDat, tongTien FROM dbo.DonHang WHERE khachHangId = 42 AND YEAR(ngayDat) = 2025 ORDER BY ngayDat DESC on 50,000 orders that have only a primary key (661 logical reads, Sort + Clustered Index Scan).

  1. Create ix_kh_ngay so that this query becomes one Index Seek with no lookup and no sort.
  2. Create dbo.prDonHangTrongNam @kh INT, @nam INT returning the same rows, newest first, with a SARGable year condition.

check.sql compares your procedure with the original query for three customers and reads its logical reads from sys.dm_exec_procedure_stats: it must read at most 30 pages (the original reads 661).

Runs on YOUR SQL Server, not in the browser. The point is the page count on a 50,000-row table: only a real SQL Server can show that the plan changed (here measured with sys.dm_exec_procedure_stats.last_logical_reads). Nothing here is graded automatically: run the self-check check.sql on your machine and, when it prints ALL 5 CHECKS PASSED, press Mark as solved.

How to run it (Windows or macOS)

Press Tải .zip (download) above the code and unzip it. The folder has three files: setup.sql (re-creates a scratch database DBI202_CL with the sample tables), solution.sql (YOUR answer — edit only this one) and check.sql (5 checks; prints PASS/FAIL for each and ends with ALL 5 CHECKS PASSED). Always run them in this order: setup → solution → check.

  • Windows + SSMS (the course setup, lesson 0.3): open setup.sql → F5; open solution.sql → F5; open check.sql → F5, then read the Messages tab. Or in a terminal inside the folder (sqlcmd ships with SQL Server; otherwise winget install sqlcmd):
    sqlcmd -S localhost -E -C -i setup.sql,solution.sql,check.sql (use -U sa -P "<password>" instead of -E for a SQL login).
  • macOS (SQL Server in Docker, as in lesson 0.3 — Apple Silicon: mcr.microsoft.com/azure-sql-edge, Intel: mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2022-latest):
    docker run -d --name dbi202-sql -e ACCEPT_EULA=Y -e "MSSQL_SA_PASSWORD=Dbi202#Lab" -p 1433:1433 mcr.microsoft.com/azure-sql-edge
    then install the command-line client once with brew install sqlcmd and, inside the folder:
    sqlcmd -S localhost,1433 -U sa -P "Dbi202#Lab" -C -i setup.sql,solution.sql,check.sql
    (or open the three files in VS Code with the SQL Server (mssql) extension and run them in the same order).

Use CREATE OR ALTER for procedures, functions, triggers and views so that you can run solution.sql again and again. In the real PE you submit only the CREATE … statement, without GO or test commands.

Requirements

  • Index: equality column, then range/sort column, INCLUDE what the SELECT needs.
  • Procedure: no YEAR()/DATEPART()/CONVERT() on ngayDat — use DATEFROMPARTS(@nam, 1, 1) and DATEFROMPARTS(@nam + 1, 1, 1).

  • macOS (SQL Server trong Docker như bài 0.3 — Apple Silicon: mcr.microsoft.com/azure-sql-edge, Intel: mcr.microsoft.com/mssql/server:2022-latest):

-- Step 3: the year as a half-open range, so ngayDat stays bare (SARGable)
CREATE OR ALTER PROCEDURE dbo.prDonHangTrongNam @kh INT, @nam INT
AS
BEGIN
    SET NOCOUNT ON;
    SELECT id, maDon, ngayDat, tongTien
    FROM dbo.DonHang
    WHERE khachHangId = @kh
      AND ngayDat >= DATEFROMPARTS(@nam, 1, 1)
      AND ngayDat <  DATEFROMPARTS(@nam + 1, 1, 1)
    ORDER BY ngayDat DESC;
END
